clue.text: Main attribute of the House?

parts.note: read as a property of a home: the supply it draws from the mains pipe in the street, not a quality of the parliamentary House

explanation.surface: A question about the defining feature of the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'chief', and 'the House' like Parliament; in fact the main is the pipe under the street feeding a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary household supply drawn from the mains is what comes out of the kitchen faucet.

clue.text: Channel with fish, fed by river

indicators.note: fed by means supplied with something put into it, so the river abbreviation goes inside the fish

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A waterway stocked with fish is supplied by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch or channel dug in the ground.

clue.text: Dog died in southern English resort

indicators.note: in here places the death abbreviation within the name of the resort

parts.note: Poole is a seaside town in Dorset, on England's south coast
d. is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A dog passes away at a seaside town in the south of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The poodle is a curly-coated breed of dog.

clue.text: Fished with line on Dee

parts.note: an angle is a line of approach or point of view, as in 'take a new angle'
dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D

explanation.surface: Someone fished with rod and line on the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a salmon river in Scotland and Wales, but here 'Dee' is just the letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with hook and line, so angled is fished.

clue.text: It gets one quite put out

definitions.text: It gets one quite put out

parts.words: It gets one quite put out
parts.note: read not as being annoyed but as a fire being put out completely, quenched

explanation.surface: Something that leaves a person thoroughly annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' suggests irritated; it is the literal sense of a flame being smothered.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuff a fire or light is to quench it fully, putting it out.

clue.text: Object received by prelate gratefully, but returned

indicators.note: the run held inside those words is read backwards, coming back the other way
the words prelate gratefully take in, or hold, the letters needed

explanation.surface: A bishop gratefully accepts something and then gives it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received by' points inside 'prelate gratefully', where TEGRAT sits across the join; 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An object in the sense of an aim or goal is what one shoots for.

clue.text: A hamper, the worse for wear, stuffed with old jars

indicators.note: stuffed with means filled by, so the old abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
something the worse for wear is battered out of shape, so the letters of a hamper are rearranged

explanation.surface: A battered picnic basket is filled with antique pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the worse for wear' reshapes A HAMPER into AMPHRAE, and 'stuffed with' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphorae are tall two-handled jars used in ancient Greece and Rome.

clue.text: Language source — Inca, maybe

parts.note: a germ is the source or origin of something, as the germ of an idea

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word Inca could take another form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The origin of a language might be the Inca tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inca, maybe' looks like an example; 'maybe' rearranges INCA to ANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Germanic is the language family including English, German and Dutch.

clue.text: Walking in the northern university town

parts.note: in northern English dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
Reading is a town in Berkshire with a university

explanation.surface: Walking around a university town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northern' looks like a direction; it marks the dialect form t' for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is to walk or step, so treading is walking.

clue.text: English lag, note, involved in stretch

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of lag and note are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An English convict and a written message are caught up in a prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lag' (a convict) and 'stretch' (a jail term) suggest prison; 'involved' rearranges LAG NOTE into LONGATE after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch something is to make it longer, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Southern purification plant

parts.note: a purge is a cleansing or purification

explanation.surface: A cleansing works in the south of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' reads as a factory or works; it is a garden plant, the euphorbia.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurge is the common name for euphorbia, a genus of flowering herbs.

clue.text: Irish girls in Hebridean isle seen cavorting

parts.note: Coll is an island of the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland

indicators.note: cavorting means prancing about, so the letters of seen jump into a new order

explanation.surface: Young Irish women are spotted frolicking on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Colleen is the Irish word for a girl or young woman, from Irish cailín.

clue.text: County division shown in yellow

parts.note: a ward is an electoral division of a town or county

explanation.surface: A local government area is marked on a map in yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' looks like a colour on a map; it means cowardly, used as a noun-like answer here.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and a yellow-belly is a person lacking courage.

clue.text: Girl's butter I spread

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, here with its possessive s

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters of butter and I are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl says she is spreading her butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' both rearranges BUTTER I into TRIBUTE after DIS and, read with the whole clue, defines the answer: spreading butter is dealing it out over the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter is dealt out over bread when spread, the sense of sharing out.

clue.text: Cut for the Italian, splitting change

indicators.note: splitting means breaking apart, so the Italian article is put into the middle of the word for change

parts.note: a mutation is a change
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: A cut made for an Italian divides people on the question of change.
explanation.walkthrough: IL goes into MUTATION after its first four letters: MUT-IL-ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutilation is a severe cutting or maiming of a body or text.

clue.text: Get daughter to sing a breathtaking passage?

parts.note: to win something is to get or gain it
to pipe is to sing in a high voice, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Have your daughter sing a stunning musical passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathtaking passage' sounds like a stunning bit of music; it is the tube that takes breath in.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the airway that carries breath to the lungs.

clue.text: Female robe in trunk

parts.note: Sara is a female name
a toga is a Roman robe

explanation.surface: A woman's robe is packed in a trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: A saratoga trunk is a large domed travelling trunk named after Saratoga Springs, New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A saratoga is a large travelling chest with a rounded lid.

clue.text: Not the place for a bungalow

definitions.text: Not the place for a bungalow

parts.words: Not the place for a bungalow
parts.note: a bungalow is a single-storey house, so it has no higher floor

explanation.surface: A remark about where one should not build a single-storey house.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a building site; a bungalow has only a ground floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The rooms on a higher floor are exactly what a single-storey house lacks.

clue.text: Out of place, a pipe is not functioning

indicators.note: read as 'not functioning', the words a pipe is not are out of order and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A pipe that has stopped working is in the wrong place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not functioning' reads as one phrase, but 'not' is fodder: rearrange A PIPE IS NOT, with 'functioning' (working into new shape) as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inappropriate or unsuitable remarks are said to be out of place.

clue.text: Wager everyone's captivated by dance performance

indicators.note: captivated by means held captive inside, so the word for everyone goes within the wager

parts.note: a bet is a wager
all means everyone; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Everyone is enthralled by a gamble on a dance show.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet is a theatrical dance performed to music.

clue.text: Burrower circling dry spot

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the burrower surrounds the letters for dry

parts.note: a mole is an animal that burrows underground
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, dry

explanation.surface: A mole digs round a patch of dry ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' gives TT, teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: To mottle is to mark with spots or blotches of colour.

clue.text: State is promoting ball game

indicators.note: promoting means pushing forward, so the state is placed ahead of is

parts.note: Tenn. is the abbreviation for Tennessee, a US state
taken as written

explanation.surface: A state is backing a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a game played with rackets and a ball over a net.

clue.text: Sketches — drawings — from what we hear

indicators.note: this phrase says the word is taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: draughts are drawings, as of beer from the cask or air into a room

explanation.surface: Sketches and drawings are described from hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawings' looks like a synonym for sketches; it is the British DRAUGHTS (drawings of liquid or air), which sounds like DRAFTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Drafts are rough preliminary sketches or versions.

clue.text: Fake rejected — a unique red opal

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for fake is read backwards

parts.note: to rig something, such as an election, is to fake its result
sole means one and only, unique

explanation.surface: A forgery is turned down: this red opal is one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns RIG into GIR, then A and SOLE follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Girasole is a fire opal, showing red or orange reflections.

clue.text: Club I caricatured initially, being satirical

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of caricatured is used

explanation.surface: A golf club caricatured me, in a mocking way.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is the satirist's tool, saying the opposite of what is meant to mock.

clue.text: Flash from missile, burning

parts.note: a bullet is a missile fired from a gun
a fire that is in is still burning

explanation.surface: A flash from a burning missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' reads as a burst of light; it is a news flash.
explanation.definitionFit: A news flash is a brief urgent report or announcement.

clue.text: "Pass" from bridge player having to decline

parts.note: East, E, is one of the four players at bridge
a lapse is a decline or falling off in standard

explanation.surface: A bridge player says 'pass' because the hand has gone downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' sounds like a bridge call; it is the verb, as time passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse or pass by, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Presents unusually jaunty quality

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters of presents take an odd order

explanation.surface: Gifts with an unusually perky character.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertness is cheeky liveliness, a jaunty or saucy manner.
